item.title: Confidential Computing Built into EC2 Instances (Sponsor)
item.description: Every security review asks: what can the cloud provider access? The AWS Nitro System was built with no operator access, and no code changes required:🚫 No operator access by design: No system or person can log in to Nitro hosts, read instance memory, or access customer data on encrypted EBS volumes.📋 Authenticated, audited APIs only: Even AWS's most privileged operators are limited to authorized, audited APIs, none of which can access customer data.⚡ Near bare-metal performance: The Nitro Hypervisor performs like bare metal for most workloads, so isolation doesn't cost throughput.Learn how the AWS Nitro System delivers confidential computing →

item.title: Introducing Harness AI Budgets (5 minute read)
item.description: Harness AI Budgets turns AI cost policies into enforced weekly spending limits scoped to a team, developer, model, or project. Access pauses at 100% until the weekly reset or an approved increase. In Harness' internal test, weekly AI spend per developer fell about 37%.

item.title: Critical PHP RCE Vulnerabilities: Patch Now (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) (5 minute read)
item.description: Two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in PHP, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, were publicly disclosed on October 21. Proof-of-concept exploit code is available, and the flaws affect every PHP version from PHP 5 onward. DigitalOcean is automatically patching WordPress instances on its Cloudways managed product, but customers running PHP on Droplets or other unmanaged services must update to PHP 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, or 8.5.12 immediately. There are no patches for PHP 8.1 or earlier.

item.title: ObservabilityCON 2026: A guide to all the announcements from Grafana Labs (10 minute read)
item.description: Grafana Labs announced Grafana Cloud updates covering AI operations, cost controls, and full-stack context. Assistant Watchers reached general availability, Adaptive Telemetry customers report cutting spend 30% to 50% on average, and the Grafana Marketplace launched with more than 30 plugins.

item.title: Scaling GitOps With Release Promotion (4 minute read)
item.description: Jesse Suen of Akuity describes a fleet of over 200 clusters where every merge synced everywhere with no gate. He argues sync tools do not handle release tracking or promotion decisions and recommends staged promotion that rolls out in waves and halts on failed checks.

item.title: I Don't Trust ON DELETE CASCADE (6 minute read)
item.description: Large cascading deletes can turn a routine schema migration into an outage by holding locks while new queries queue behind the waiting migration. Soft deletes followed by bounded background cleanup keep transactions smaller, with additional pitfalls around unindexed foreign keys and logical replication.

item.title: Presentation: AI is an Amplifier: Scale High Performance, Not Dysfunction (33 minute read)
item.description: Nathen Harvey of Google Cloud's DORA team presents 2025 survey findings from nearly 5,000 respondents, about 90% of whom use AI professionally. He argues AI amplifies existing organizational strengths and dysfunctions, and introduces the DORA AI Capabilities Model.

item.title: JEV helps your agent decide what to do next. Bluehost gives it somewhere to run 24/7. (Sponsor)
item.description: Your agent shouldn't depend on your laptop staying open. Run it on an always-on VPS with a 99.99% uptime guarantee, so it keeps working after you log offGet started

item.title: Claude-How-To (GitHub Repo)
item.description: This MIT-licensed guide teaches users how to use Claude Code through 10 modules covering slash commands, hooks, skills, and MCP servers. Users can copy templates directly into projects or follow a self-assessment quiz to get a personalized roadmap. The current version, v2.1.302, is compatible with Claude Code 2.1+ and includes copy-paste templates for models including Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5.

item.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Lockfiles in Public Preview (2 minute read)
item.description: GitHub Actions workflow lockfiles pin actions and their transitive dependencies to reviewed commits while preserving readable tags in workflow files. The public preview includes a GitHub CLI extension to generate lockfiles, Dependabot integration to update them, and policies that require workflows to use them.

item.title: 8 eMudhra certificates are compromised. Here's what you need to know (4 minute read)
item.description: Private keys for eight widely trusted eMudhra intermediate certificates were compromised on October 19, allowing attackers to forge certificates for any domain. Cloudflare has patched its CDN, Zero Trust, and Tunnel products. Customers must update the Cloudflare One Client and 1.1.1.1 app to specific versions to remain protected.

item.title: Before you evaluate an AI SRE, give your existing agent context (6 minute read)
item.description: Engineers at Radar tested whether adding context to coding agents improves Kubernetes diagnostics. When running 50 fault scenarios, agents with context reached a correct diagnosis within two minutes on 86% of faults, compared to 60% for agents using a standard shell. Accuracy improved only slightly with context, but the time savings were significant. The test used Claude Code and Microsoft's SREGym benchmark on a live Amazon EKS cluster.

item.title: GitHub Actions Runner Controller 0.15.0 Targets Reliability at Scale (3 minute read)
item.description: GitHub released Actions Runner Controller 0.15.0, which sends smaller patch requests and moves runner status aggregation into metrics to reduce Kubernetes API updates.

item.title: AI infrastructure on tap with the Pulumi AICR provider (3 minute read)
item.description: Pulumi has released the NVIDIA AI Cluster Runtime (AICR) provider to help developers deploy self-hosted AI infrastructure.

item.title: Gartner's DevSecOps Magic Quadrant Rates Atlassian as the Top Vendor in “Ability to Execute” (Sponsor)
item.description: Atlassian has been named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for DevSecOps Platforms for the fourth consecutive year.>> The global research positioned Atlassian's ability to execute as top amongst vendors reviewed – including Microsoft, GitLab, and Harness. >> Atlassian was also ranked among the top organizations for completeness of vision.Read the DevSecOps Magic Quadrant to get the full picture why Atlassian has emerged as a consistent leader in DevSecOps – and how your team can use Atlassian tools to deliver secure execution across every stage of the development lifecycle. Get your free copy

item.title: Stack Overflow for Agents triples signups with ChatGPT plugin (3 minute read)
item.description: Stack Overflow built Stack Overflow for Agents in a few weeks with two engineers using Codex. A ChatGPT plugin reportedly tripled overnight registrations, and Codex cut enterprise connector build time from 3 to 6 weeks to 4 days.

item.title: Introducing Amazon ECS Gateway: A fully-managed ingress solution for ECS services (4 minute read)
item.description: Amazon ECS Gateway is a resource that simplifies ingress networking for containerized workloads by automatically provisioning load balancers and certificates. It allows up to 25 services to share a single Application Load Balancer to optimize infrastructure costs. Amazon ECS Gateway is available now in all commercial AWS Regions at no additional charge, though users pay for the underlying resources provisioned in their accounts.

item.title: Introducing tsrs: a Port of TypeScript to Rust (5 minute read)
item.description: Cloudflare and VoidZero are collaborating on tsrs, a Rust port of the TypeScript compiler. Early benchmarks show tsrs is up to 8x faster and uses roughly 70% less memory than TypeScript 7.0. The team is working with the TypeScript team to ensure the port remains compatible with the official language design. Rust allows the compiler to run in WebAssembly, which enables development environments to run in browsers or on embedded devices.

item.title: Redesigning Source Control at Anthropic (15 minute read)
item.description: Anthropic replaced Git for its monorepo with Scion, a centralized source control system designed for tens of millions of daily CI checkouts. Content-addressed storage, server-side repository operations, and tiered caches reduced its source-control CPU and memory footprint 200× compared with its previous Git mirroring infrastructure.

item.title: AI agents vs. Kubernetes: where each belongs in the control loop (6 minute read)
item.description: Kubernetes operators suit deterministic reconciliation, while AI agents suit goals with unclear paths, according to a CNCF-sponsored piece. Use an observe, diagnose, propose, approve, reconcile, and verify loop, with autonomy phased from read-only investigation to approved low-risk changes.

item.title: SIMD and Go (20 minute read)
item.description: Go's experimental SIMD packages expose vector instructions that process multiple values in one operation without handwritten assembly. Examples cover vector registers, loads, arithmetic, and compiler behavior using Go 1.27's experimental SIMD support on amd64.

item.title: What it actually takes to build an AI SRE (Sponsor)
item.description: Two years, hundreds of prompts, one adversarial agent. Here's what it really took us to build incident.io Investigations, and why the prototype is a trap. Read More →

item.title: Headroom (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Headroom compresses tool outputs, logs, files, and RAG chunks before they reach the LLM. Benchmarks show the compression results in 20% fewer tokens for coding agents and 60-95% fewer tokens for JSON. The tool runs locally to ensure no prompt or file content is sent externally.

item.title: vLLM (GitHub Repo)
item.description: vLLM is a library for LLM inference and serving that originated in the Sky Computing Lab at UC Berkeley. The open-source project now has over 2,000 contributors and supports more than 200 model architectures on Hugging Face.

item.title: Cutting Our Inference Bill by 68% Through Optimization (15 minute read)
item.description: Cloudflare reduced its AI code reviewer's average cost from $2.43 to $0.77 through shared prompt-cache prefixes, fewer redundant tool calls, and model and reasoning-effort changes. Median review time fell from 4 minutes 9 seconds to 1 minute 32 seconds, while quality checks exposed trade-offs where cheaper configurations missed important findings.

item.title: Inside Prometheus: Meta's Journey to a Gigawatt-Scale Supercluster (13 minute read)
item.description: Meta is building Prometheus, a gigawatt-scale supercluster in New Albany, Ohio, that will eventually comprise roughly 1 million GPUs. The first phase of the project has already trained the company's Muse foundational models. Meta achieved over 85% goodput for pre-training runs and reduced interruption rates by 99% from their peak. The cluster currently deploys NVIDIA GB200 and GB300 platforms, with plans to integrate the upcoming Vera Rubin NVL72 next.

item.title: Reach 8 million tech professionals reading TLDR (Sponsor)
item.description: Ads get ignored on social media but not in TLDR! Reach DevOps and platform engineers where they actually pay attention. Learn more about sponsorship opportunities.

item.title: How Itaú is building generative AI for its entire customer base (7 minute read)
item.description: Itaú is applying its AI-first strategy using OpenAI models, including the ia.i assistant that reached about 300,000 customers in its first phase.

item.title: Announcing Wiz Runtime Sensor add-on for GKE: Turnkey threat detection for Kubernetes (5 minute read)
item.description: Google Cloud and Wiz released the Wiz Runtime Sensor add-on for GKE in preview.

item.title: Learn Why Forrester Just Named Atlassian a Leader in Conversational AI Platforms for Employee Services (Sponsor)
item.description: Atlassian was recognized as a Leader in The Forrester Wave™: Conversational AI Platforms for Employee Services, Q3 2026, with their “strength of strategy” and “strength of offering” ranking them as outliers in the field. Here's some of what Forrester had to say:Strategy: Atlassian “is prioritizing connected user context across tools, proactive employee support, and embedding Rovo where people work.”Capabilities: “Atlassian stands out for its context capabilities and ability to embed Rovo into key collaborative surfaces.”Forrester's take: “Atlassian's agent is ideal for existing customers and those that want to automate more service experiences and experiment with cross-vendor agents.”Get the report.

item.title: Cloudflare and OpenAI: making AI discovery better for everyone (5 minute read)
item.description: A research pilot between Cloudflare and OpenAI has enabled the discovery and indexing of hundreds of millions of new web pages. The program used signals from roughly 1% of Cloudflare's network to help ChatGPT find content that was previously unknown. These signals identify useful pages and filter out nonexistent or duplicated content, which reduces unnecessary crawling load for site owners. Cloudflare states the metadata is used for search discovery rather than training AI models.

item.title: Claude Platform Tracing in New Relic (4 minute read)
item.description: The Claude Platform now exports OpenTelemetry traces natively from Claude Managed Agents, the Messages API, and the Claude SDKs in public beta. New Relic AI Monitoring reads these traces to link model performance with application data in a single view. Users can add New Relic as a destination in the Claude Console to start receiving spans within about a minute without code changes.

item.title: Introducing Scout 1.0: A new SRE model powering Bits AI with frontier performance at a fraction of the cost (4 minute read)
item.description: Datadog's Scout 1.0 is an AI model specialized for investigating production issues that powers its Bits AI assistant. The model matches the performance of general-purpose frontier models like GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5 at three to eight times lower estimated inference cost. Datadog trained Scout using reinforcement learning on simulations built from historical incidents.

item.title: How Datadog Defines Service Criticality at Scale (8 minute read)
item.description: An LLM analyzed several hundred SEV-1 and SEV-2 postmortems for about USD 32 to derive four criticality signals. Services get high, low, or unknown ratings with confidence, owner overrides, and the tiers inform deployment and auto-merge decisions.

item.title: Finding (and Fixing) a Silent Throughput Ceiling in PostgreSQL (6 minute read)
item.description: PostgreSQL throughput can stall under heavy concurrent inserts even when CPU and storage have spare capacity, as writers queue behind relation extension locks. In a HammerDB benchmark, distributing writes across hash partitions reduced contention and increased throughput 7.2× on the same hardware.

item.title: Agent-first IDP: how big tech and the clouds are preparing platforms for agents (22 minute read)
item.description: This guide outlines how to evolve an internal developer platform into an Agentic Engineering Platform (AEP) suitable for AI agents. Real-world examples from Block, Uber, Spotify, and public clouds illustrate architectural decisions like managed entry points, agent identity, and trustworthy state. The playbook describes nine practices across four maturity levels, ranging from demand discovery and machine-readable contracts to policy enforcement and domain-specific agents.

item.title: Finout's new AI agents cut cloud and AI costs without burning engineering hours (Sponsor)
item.description: Trawling through dashboards and Slack threads to find wasted spend = every engineer's nightmare. Finout's AI agents (beta) do that work daily across your cloud and AI spend, then hand each owner a ready case with savings and evidence. Lower bill, higher engineering efficiency. Watch the walkthrough or book a demo.

item.title: CLI-Anything (GitHub Repo)
item.description: CLI-Anything is a tool that converts software with a codebase into command-line interfaces for AI agents. The project currently supports 18 applications, including GIMP, Blender, and LibreOffice, with 2,461 passing tests. Users can install the CLI-Hub package manager to browse and deploy these community-built CLIs.

item.title: Deploy with Void (5 minute read)
item.description: VoidZero has open-sourced Void, a toolchain that extends Vite to handle full-stack application development and deployment. The package includes an SDK, a CLI, and a Platform for teams to self-host deployment environments within their own Cloudflare accounts. It automatically provisions resources like databases and queues during deployment.

item.title: Azure Maia 300 Architecture Deep Dive (8 minute read)
item.description: Microsoft's third-generation AI accelerator uses TSMC N2P with 288 GB HBM4 at 18 TB/s. Racks hold 96 accelerators at 167 kW, scaling to 12,288-chip superpods, with up to 7x token throughput.

item.title: Atlantis at Scale (13 minute read)
item.description: Details running Atlantis v0.47.1 as a single-replica StatefulSet with Redis locking and S3 plan storage. Limits include an alpha drift API with no scheduler and no cross-project dependency graph. Spacelift positions itself as the alternative.

item.title: Signals & Levers: Systems Thinking Tools to Unblock Software Delivery (Sponsor)
item.description: Metrics look green, but releases keep slipping. Elisabeth Hendrickson and Joel Tosi show how to separate signal from noise, map why fixes backfire, and find levers that actually unblock delivery.Get the book

item.title: Amazon ECS Adds LiveTaskCount Service Metric (1 minute read)
item.description: A free metric counts tasks that are activating, running, or deactivating, without Container Insights.

item.title: Powering European Scientific Discovery with Advanced AI Compute (1 minute read)
item.description: Google DeepMind and Google Cloud will give up to 200 European researchers access to AlphaFold 3, WeatherNext, and other models, plus USD 3 million in compute credits.

item.title: Spacelift Integrates with Cursor Origin (3 minute read)
item.description: Agent-driven infrastructure changes now flow through Spacelift using a registered Origin app with a signing key, so the same OPA policies and approvals apply. A cited report says 76% would apply AI-generated Terraform with little review.

item.title: Cloudflare Logpush Transformers (7 minute read)
item.description: Cloudflare Transformers use SQL to filter, redact, and reshape logs before export. The feature is now generally available on all plans.

item.title: Amazon S3 is now available on the Vercel Marketplace and v0 by Vercel (4 minute read)
item.description: Developers on Vercel can now provision Amazon S3 storage, including S3 Tables and S3 Vectors, directly from the Vercel Marketplace and v0. The integration handles connection configuration automatically and supports three workloads: everyday storage, analytics, and AI. Users pay standard Amazon S3 pricing for the resources they use, and new AWS accounts created through Vercel receive $100 in credits valid for six months.

item.title: Sequences and Other Volatiles in Neki (12 minute read)
item.description: Distributing PostgreSQL queries across shards gets complicated when functions depend on time or generate sequence values. Neki coordinates sequence allocation through its router and preserves how often expressions execute, preventing query optimizations from producing duplicate IDs or changing SQL behavior.

item.title: Inside Hyperdrive: How We Solved a Rare MySQL Caching Bug (10 minute read)
item.description: A rare Hyperdrive bug returned empty MySQL results when two components shared a cache but encoded responses using different protocol capabilities. Cloudflare traced the failures to an assumption inherited from its Postgres implementation and fixed them by storing responses in a canonical format before translating them for each client.

item.title: What happens when you rebuild Redis for multi-core hardware? (Sponsor)
item.description: Redis runs one core per process. Your server has 64. Dragonfly is a multi-threaded, Redis/Valkey-compatible data store built by an ex-AWS ElastiCache engineer. It hits 6M ops/sec on a single node, no cluster needed. Instacart used it to cut latency in half on 70% fewer nodes. Learn more

item.title: Tokenspeed (GitHub Repo)
item.description: TokenSpeed is an open-source LLM inference engine designed for agentic workloads, offering TensorRT-LLM-level performance and vLLM-level usability. It is the first inference engine to separate the control plane, implemented in C++, from the execution plane, implemented in Python. The project is backed by the non-profit LightSeek Foundation with support from vendors including NVIDIA and AMD.

item.title: Xerj (GitHub Repo)
item.description: XERJ is a local AI search tool that indexes code, docs, logs, and PDFs for search and RAG. It uses 40x fewer tokens than grep and reduces a coding agent's output tokens by 2.7x in controlled studies. The tool is compatible with the Elasticsearch API and runs on Linux, macOS, and Windows.

item.title: Improving Developer Productivity with New Relic AI (6 minute read)
item.description: Shows production telemetry reaching AI coding agents over MCP. Examples cover Claude Code deployment health reports, Kiro right-sizing, a Copilot action that finds observability gaps, and an incident response agent. The MCP server lists 3 skills and 42 tools.

item.title: Pulumi ESC now issues OIDC tokens for any service (5 minute read)
item.description: Pulumi ESC environments can now mint short-lived OpenID Connect (OIDC) tokens for any service that accepts one. The new fn::open::oidc provider generates tokens that expire within one hour, eliminating the security risks associated with storing long-lived API keys. Developers can use these tokens to authenticate with services like Anthropic, Cloudsmith, JFrog Artifactory, and Aembit without storing static credentials. The feature is available now in every Pulumi Cloud organization.

item.title: A Container Image Can Be Vulnerability-Free and Still Not Trustworthy (5 minute read)
item.description: A clean scan only covers known CVEs, while malicious code like the Nx Console compromise needs none.

item.title: One Agent Development Kit, Five Languages (6 minute read)
item.description: ADK now covers Python, Go, TypeScript, Java, and Kotlin, all with MCP and A2A support.

item.description: Atlassian's AI-native ITSM helps every team deliver exceptional service experiences. item.title: SRE book second edition (3 minute read)
item.description: Google has released a completely rewritten second edition of its Site Reliability Engineering book with O'Reilly Media. The update reflects a decade of changes to the reliability field, including the rise of AI, microservices, and platform engineering. The new text includes guidance on modern challenges like running large language models and using AI to enhance operational reliability.

item.title: Announcing AWS Lambda Web Functions (5 minute read)
item.description: AWS Lambda Web Functions is a new form factor that runs standard HTTP web applications without rewriting code into an event handler. Developers can deploy existing Node.js servers built with frameworks like Express or Next.js, and the service automatically handles scaling and multi-region distribution. Each execution environment handles up to 128 concurrent requests, and billing is based on active CPU time rather than total duration. It is available today in five regions.

item.title: AKS Is Growing – Along With Its Kubernetes Utilization Problem (5 minute read)
item.description: Per the 2026 State of Kubernetes Optimization Report, AKS CPU utilization fell to 8% and memory to 20%, with CPU overprovisioning at 69%. GPU utilization averages 5% overall and 2% on AKS, driven by conservative resource requests that are rarely revisited.

item.title: Under the hood, off the hot path: How D1 scales to millions of databases (24 minute read)
item.description: Cloudflare scaled D1's control plane to manage millions of SQLite-backed databases while keeping centralized components out of the query hot path. Distributed routing metadata, pooled Postgres connections, precomputed aggregations, and idempotent background processes reduce bottlenecks as database counts grow.

item.title: Headless Observability: The Next Evolution of Autonomous Operations (6 minute read)
item.description: New Relic argues observability must evolve for AI agents as well as humans, since agents need trusted operational intelligence rather than raw telemetry. Its Ground Truth layer combines telemetry, relationships, evidence, and context, separating intelligence from presentation so dashboards and APIs serve both audiences.

item.title: Fastest Growing Open Source Datadog Alternative (Sponsor)
item.description: Open source, unified observability platform with ~22.3k GitHub stars, 10k+ deployments, and migration in 30 minutes. No host fees. No custom metric fees. No overages. Store in your S3. OTel-native logs, metrics, traces and RUM. Start for free with Cloud or self-host.

item.title: Voicestudio (GitHub Repo)
item.description: VoiceStudio is an open-source alternative to ElevenLabs that runs fully locally on user hardware. The software supports voice cloning, video dubbing, transcription, and audiobook creation in 646 languages.

item.title: Xtool (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Xtool is a cross-platform tool that replicates Xcode functionality using open standards. It lets developers build and deploy iOS apps on Linux, Windows, and macOS. The tool can sign, install, and interact with Apple Developer Services programmatically.

item.title: What gets TOASTed in Postgres (12 minute read)
item.description: Postgres TOAST compresses oversized variable-length values and moves them into separate storage when necessary. SQL examples show why LZ4's faster compression does not always produce smaller values or faster reads: pglz can outperform it for short previews, while uncompressed external storage can improve reads from the middle of large binary values.

item.title: Shipping Media Over QUIC at Meta Scale for Instagram Live Ingest (6 minute read)
item.description: Instagram Live now uses the open standard Media over QUIC (MoQ) protocol for live video ingest on iOS and Android. This switch moves development from Meta's in-house RUSH protocol to a shared IETF standard developed with Google, Akamai, and others. Meta says the MoQ path matched RUSH on streaming quality and reliability measures during testing.

item.title: Frontier security AI, compressed to run on prem (Sponsor)
item.description: Aikido built Altar, an open-weight model that maintains 92% vulnerability coverage at a third of the size. Learn more →

item.title: Rewinding the exponential: How we keep hardware usage down (12 minute read)
item.description: Cloudflare reduced data-pipeline traffic by moving replication downstream and applying sampling and aggregation earlier.

item.title: Stop rewriting the same update with AI-Powered Incident Communications (3 minute read)
item.description: PagerDuty's AI-powered Incident Communications, now in rolling general availability, uses Scribe Agent to capture bridge audio and chat across Zoom, Teams, and Meet.

item.title: New AI Special Interest Group (1 minute read)
item.description: The CD Foundation launched an AI Special Interest Group on defining how AI fits into CI/CD, with its first meeting on October 7 and biweekly sessions after.
